Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates lucent streaks of air tracking along the mediastinal structures, particularly visible as vertical radiolucencies adjacent to the heart and great vessels (continuous diaphragm sign), which is characteristic of pneumomediastinum. This pattern, especially when prominent anteriorly and extending into the neck without significant pleural effusion or hydropneumothorax, is most consistent with alveolar rupture (Macklin effect) rather than esophageal perforation (Boerhaave syndrome), which typically presents with left-sided pleural effusion and more severe systemic toxicity.
